about: omher's one masker for token-like text: the bridge (mask_secrets), the desktop shell (tasks.rs mask_secrets) and the page (src/lib/secrets.ts) all use these patterns, and secrets.cases.json holds the table all three test against. `split` goes first: a family with a fixed body length (ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_: 36 of [A-Za-z0-9]; glpat-: 20 of [A-Za-z0-9_-]) broken by up to four line breaks or single spaces, in any letter case. Each entry is [pattern, length]; group 1 is the body's pieces, which are counted in order, and when they make exactly `length` characters at the end of a piece the prefix and those pieces are replaced by `mask` (the pieces after stay). Otherwise the text is left for `tokens`. `tokens` is replaced whole by `mask`; it also takes a token broken by line breaks or a space (up to four breaks), joining a next piece only when that piece is token-shaped (two or more capitals or digits), so a prose word after the break stays. `assigned` (case-insensitive) keeps its name and `=` and replaces the value.
